name: Katherine Gorge
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage See/Do and Tourism NT both name it as the headline Katherine attraction; cruises, canoes, walks and a swim, well over half an hour. Free entry to the park.
objection: It is the same draw as the Nitmiluk National Park spot (park boat and walks); placement should merge or distinguish them (gorge departure point vs park), or it is a near-duplicate under rule 3.

name: Jatbula Trail
reason: Rule 1 x2 (Wikivoyage, Tourism NT page): 58 km, 4-6 day DOC-style great walk, a benchmark-type multi-day track like Hump Ridge.
objection: Needs a permit and a ferry hop, so few visitors do it; still named in two counted sources.

name: Sweetwater Pool
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage plus a Tourism NT page name it; a swimming hole at the end of an 8.6 km return walk from Leliyn, so a half-day.
objection: Part of the Edith Falls/Leliyn walking network and a destination of a walk, not a separate draw; only one real guide listing.

name: Southern Rockhole
reason: Rule 1 x2: Wikivoyage uses it as the Katherine page header image and Tourism NT lists it; a swimming waterhole.
objection: It lies on the Jatbula Trail (rule 3: part of a larger spot) and is not a stop most day visitors reach.

name: Northern Rockhole
reason: Rule 3: a seasonal waterfall and lunch spot within Nitmiluk, one source, no distinct visit.
objection: Tourism NT does list it as a thing to do; but flowing only early dry season and part of the park.

name: Nitmiluk Visitor Centre
reason: Rule 2: a service/ticket building, not a place to see.
objection: Tourism NT lists it; but it is where Nitmiluk Tours depart, which the Katherine Gorge spot already covers.

name: Keep River National Park
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT page; a national park with sandstone formations and walks. A second-tier park a guide recommends.
objection: One counted source; remote on the WA border. A Parks NT page is blocked, so not independently confirmed.

name: Goorrandalng Walk
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT names it; 2 km walk among sculpted sandstone (about an hour).
objection: Part of Keep River National Park (rule 3), one source; the park spot already stands for it.

name: Jarnem Lookout Walk
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT names it; 7 km splittable loop to a lookout with a half-day visit.
objection: Part of Keep River National Park (rule 3), single source, tiny audience.

name: Limmen National Park
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT page; large national park (9,370 sq km) with river, wetlands and sandstone formations.
objection: Remote, 4WD-oriented and sparse visitor infrastructure; one counted source.

name: Southern Lost City
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT names it; sandstone spires with a 2 km loop, about an hour.
objection: Single source, 35 km off the highway on a gravel road; may be just part of Limmen National Park.

name: Western Lost City
reason: Rule 2: 28 km high-clearance 4WD track plus a gate key from a ranger station; effectively inaccessible to most visitors.
objection: Tourism NT names it and the formations are reputed to be spectacular.

name: Butterfly Springs
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT names it as the park's only safe swim plus campground in Limmen.
objection: Single source and mostly a campground; part of the Limmen National Park draw.

name: Mataranka Thermal Pools
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage describes it as the Mataranka headline (palm-fringed 34 C lagoon) and it is a swimming stop on the Explorer's Way.
objection: Inside Elsey National Park (the kept park spot) so could be counted as part of it; but the pool is the named draw and a distinct place.

name: Bitter Springs
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT page (opened, 200); natural thermal spring with an accessible path, a distinct swim from the pools at Mataranka.
objection: Near-duplicate of Mataranka Thermal Pools in appeal and closed in the wet season; single counted source.

name: Riverside Walk
reason: Rule 3: a 16 km walk within Elsey National Park, already covered by the park spot; one source.
objection: Tourism NT names it as a scenic walk.

name: Botanic Walk
reason: Rule 3: a 1.5 km walk inside Elsey National Park, one source, covered by the park.
objection: Named by Tourism NT.

name: Old Mataranka Sheep Dip
reason: Rule 3: a minor heritage fragment in Elsey National Park, a ten-minute look.
objection: Tourism NT lists it as a historical site.

name: Mataranka
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage lists Mataranka as a township with barramundi feeding and a museum, the base for the pools and Elsey NP.
objection: The draw is the pools and park, already spots; a town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw (Wikivoyage names mostly a supermarket and campgrounds).

name: Never Never Museum
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage names it, an open museum of local Aboriginal and pioneer history (We of the Never Never) in Mataranka.
objection: Single source, a small local museum, hours unverified.

name: Stockyard Gallery
reason: Rule 2: an art shop and tea garden in Mataranka; a retail venue.
objection: Wikivoyage names it with barramundi feeding tours.

name: Douglas Hot Springs
reason: Rule 1 x2 (Wikivoyage, Tourism NT): a natural hot spring park with a 31 C pool, a swimming stop.
objection: Remote, 130 km north of Katherine on a gravel road, and the main pool is a short visit.

name: Cutta Cutta Caves Nature Park
reason: Rule 1 x2 (Wikivoyage, Tourism NT): daily one-hour guided cave tours 27 km from Katherine.
objection: Closed in the wet season; guided tours only.

name: Umbrawarra Gorge Nature Park
reason: Rule 1 x2 (Wikivoyage Pine Creek, Tourism NT): sandy swimming holes and cliff-top views, 15 min walk from the car park.
objection: Gravel road, wet-season closures and remote.

name: Butterfly Gorge Nature Park
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT lists it; a gorge with rock pools a 10 min walk from the car park plus a lookout.
objection: Single source, reached by unsealed roads and often closed; short visit.

name: Barranyi (North Island) National Park
reason: Rule 2: an Aboriginal-owned island reached only by boat from Borroloola; not freely open to visitors.
objection: Tourism NT lists it and it resembles the Kapiti benchmark; but it needs permission and boat charter, not open whenever you arrive.

name: Caranbirini Conservation Reserve
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT page; sandstone spires known as the Lost City with a 2 km loop walk and a bird hide, about an hour.
objection: Single source, 46 km from the very remote Borroloola, and a near-twin of Southern Lost City.

name: Gregory's Tree
reason: Rule 1 x2 (Wikivoyage See, Tourism NT): the one named See item on the Gregory National Park page, a roadside heritage tree.
objection: A ten-minute roadside look and a minor historic marker; kept only because a guide singles it out by name.

name: Escarpment Walk
reason: Rule 1 x2 (Wikivoyage, Tourism NT): a 3 km, 1.5 hour trail through iconic Top End scenery.
objection: Part of the Judbarra / Gregory park spot (rule 3).

name: Calcite Flow Walk
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage names it; a 600 m, 30 minute walk over stromatolites.
objection: Single source, on a 4WD-only road 14 km past Bullita, part of the park spot.

name: Bullita Homestead
reason: Rule 3: an historic homestead that is the trailhead for the Calcite Flow Walk, in a 4WD-only part of the park; a campground rather than a draw.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Drover's Rest Boab Trees
reason: Rule 3: a roadside pull-out of boab trees; ten-minute look and no guide singles it out beyond the listing.
objection: Boabs are a photographed Top End icon.

name: Giwining Nature Park
reason: Rule 1 x2: Tourism NT and Lonely Planet (Giwining / Flora River Nature Park) name it; 25 km of spring-fed river with tufa dams and Kathleen and Djarrung Falls, 2WD dry-season access.
objection: Swimming is not allowed (crocodiles), it is 130 km out of Katherine, and it is mostly camping.

name: Timber Creek
reason: Rule 1 x2: Wikivoyage and Tourism NT name it as the Victoria River gateway town with Gregory's Tree and the old police station nearby.
objection: A tiny roadhouse town; its only draws are the park spots, so a wrapper of them.

name: Lake Copperfield
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage names it in See; a cool deep lake 6 km from Pine Creek with picnic area.
objection: Single source and a simple local swimming spot.

name: Walk Through Time
reason: Rule 3: a short footpath of painted tiles in Pine Creek, a minor civic art installation.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it; but it is a ten-minute stroll.

name: Pine Creek Water Gardens
reason: Rule 3: a small garden in a railway cutting with picnic tables, a ten-minute stop.
objection: Wikivoyage names it as a town centre feature.

name: National Trust Museum (Pine Creek)
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage calls it an excellent local-history museum in a moved 1888 building.
objection: Single source and it also houses the library; a small local museum.

name: Grove Hill Heritage Museum
reason: Rule 1 x2 (Wikivoyage, Tourism NT): a historic pub and museum on the Northern Goldfields Loop.
objection: It is a licensed hotel with camping, so the museum is a side of a hotel; a long detour.

name: Pine Creek Railway Heritage Precinct
reason: Rule 3: a railway-precinct fragment, one source; the carriage is listed separately.
objection: Tourism NT lists it as heritage.

name: NABP 13 Passenger Carriage
reason: Rule 3: a single static carriage in the Pine Creek precinct; a ten-minute look.
objection: Heritage exhibit named by Tourism NT.

name: Pine Creek Repeater Museum and Public Library
reason: Rule 2: a library-type civic building with a small museum room.
objection: Tourism NT lists it as a museum.

name: Miners Park Pine Creek
reason: Rule 3: a small park with mining displays; one source, a short look.
objection: Tourism NT lists it among heritage sites.

name: Spring Hill Battery Complex
reason: Rule 2: a mining-ruin complex with unconfirmed public access, one source.
objection: Tourism NT lists it as heritage.

name: Maranboy Mining Precinct
reason: Rule 3: a heritage mining fragment with one source and no visit detail.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Burrundie Explosive Magazines
reason: Rule 3: ruined magazine structures in the bush, a short stop with one source.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Pine Creek
reason: Rule 1 x2: Wikivoyage city article and Tourism NT destination; a historic gold town with the Water Gardens, museums and a base for Umbrawarra and Lake Copperfield.
objection: Its own draws are minor and rejected here; a town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw.

name: Top Didj Cultural Experience
reason: Rule 1 x2: Wikivoyage and Tourism NT; a paid cultural experience (talks, painting, fire lighting) 7 km from Katherine, an hour or more.
objection: A private operator and gallery shop rather than a place; the case rests on the experience being a permanent venue.

name: Katherine Art Gallery
reason: Rule 2/3: the shop at the Top Didj site, listed separately as a duplicate of Top Didj.
objection: Wikivoyage lists free entry; but it is one place with Top Didj.

name: Katherine Museum
reason: Rule 1 x2 (Wikivoyage, Tourism NT): open daily 9-4, entry $7; Overland Telegraph, Chinese-in-Territory room and a Gypsy Moth aircraft.
objection: A small regional museum; some visitors skip it.

name: Katherine School of the Air
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage names it as a living outback school visitors watch; entry fee, 101 Giles St.
objection: One counted source and lessons depend on school term; hours unverified.

name: Katherine Railway Heritage Station Precinct
reason: Rule 3: a heritage fragment with one source and no visitor detail.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Katherine Railway Trestle Bridge
reason: Rule 2: a bridge seen from the road or river; nothing to do for 30 minutes.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Fergusson River Railway Bridge and Boiler
reason: Rule 2: a bridge and boiler glanced at; one source.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Knott's Crossing
reason: Rule 3: a river crossing site at the first settlement, a plaque-level stop.
objection: Tourism NT lists it as heritage; Katherine Museum already tells the story.

name: Brocks Creek Chinatown and Temple Site
reason: Rule 2: the site of a vanished settlement; little to see.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: North Australia Railway Memorial
reason: Rule 3: a minor memorial.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Stockmans Pioneer Memorial Katherine Icon
reason: Rule 3: a roadside memorial sculpture, a few minutes.
objection: Named by Tourism NT; roadside icons are kept if a guide names them, and this is a photo stop.

name: Emungalan Cemetery
reason: Rule 2: a cemetery; no visit value.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Emungalan Wheel Shrinking Pit
reason: Rule 3: a small heritage relic, a ten-minute look.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Durack Memorial
reason: Rule 3: a minor memorial.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: WWII Hunter House
reason: Rule 2: a building with no confirmed public access.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: World War II Manbulloo Airfield Operations Centre and Abattoir
reason: Rule 2: surviving structures with unconfirmed public access, one source.
objection: Tourism NT lists it as WWII heritage.

name: Warloch Ponds Road Bridge
reason: Rule 2: a bridge seen from the roadside.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Warloch Ponds Railway Bridge
reason: Rule 2: a bridge seen from the roadside.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Frew Ponds Overland Telegraph Line Memorial Reserve
reason: Rule 3: a memorial reserve, a minor commemorative stop.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Alexander Forest Memorial
reason: Rule 3: a minor memorial.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: O'Keeffe Residence
reason: Rule 2: a private residence seen from the street.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Silver Bullets Caravans
reason: Rule 2: a commercial caravan business, not a place to see.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: The Shed Katherine
reason: Rule 1/2: purpose unclear and no visitor description found; cannot confirm what a visitor does there.
objection: Tourism NT lists it, so it may be a real venue.

name: Godinymayin Yijard Rivers Arts and Culture Centre
reason: Rule 2: an arts centre gallery and craft shop; one source.
objection: It is Aboriginal-run and a cultural venue that visitors may enjoy.

name: Merrepen Arts
reason: Rule 2: a craft and art venue with one source, closer to a shop.
objection: Aboriginal-owned arts centre of cultural interest.

name: Waralungku Arts Borroloola
reason: Rule 2: an art-centre shop in remote Borroloola, one source.
objection: Aboriginal-owned and the only gallery in Borroloola.

name: Old Borroloola Police Station Museum Heritage Precinct
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT lists it; an open museum in a former police station (1886) in Borroloola.
objection: Single source, remote, and the building is the main thing; hours unverified.

name: Seven Emu Camping Fishing
reason: Rule 2: a commercial campground and fishing site; accommodation.
objection: Tourism NT lists it.

name: Borroloola
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT Gulf Region page; the gateway town for Limmen, Caranbirini and Barranyi.
objection: Remote, with little to do in town, and its draws are the park spots (a wrapper).

name: Larrimah Museum
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT page; a small museum in Larrimah.
objection: Single source, tiny museum, hours unverified, a stop only for those passing by.

name: Larrimah
reason: Rule 3: a roadhouse township whose only listed draw is its museum, which is judged separately.
objection: Larrimah is a famous quirky outback stop (the Pink Panther pub story).

name: Daly Waters
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT destination page; a historic outback township (1930s aerodrome, the Daly Waters Pub with its beef-and-barra dinners and memorabilia), a well-known Stuart Highway stop.
objection: The listing gives no specific attraction and the core draw is a pub (a venue); it is a quirky roadside icon kept as a stop.

name: Daly River
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT destination page (opened) names the Daly River as a barramundi fishing area with tourist parks, hot springs and gorges.
objection: A large river area rather than one place; its draws are fishing and camping, with no single stop identified.

name: Savannah Way
reason: Rule 3: a touring route from Broome to Cairns, not a place (COVERAGE: a spot is a place).
objection: It is a named visitor brand, but a route cannot be visited as a spot; the places along it are judged on their own.

name: RAAF Base Tindal
reason: Not open to the public (Wikivoyage Katherine); auto-keep was on page views alone. Fails rule 2.
objection: none
